capsicum: A genus of plants of many species, producing capsules or dry berries of various forms, which have an exceedingly pungent, biting taste, and when ground form the red of Cayenne pepper of commerce. Note: The most important species are Capsicum baccatum or birs pepper. C, annuum or chili pepper, C. frutesens or spur pepper, and C.
cancriform: 1. Having the form of, or resembling, a crab; crab-shaped. 2. Like a cancer; cancerous.
carcinosys: The affection of the system with cancer.
carpophyte: A flowerless plant which forms a true fruit as the result of fertilization, as the red seaweeds, the Ascomycetes, etc. Note: The division of alge and fungi into four classes called Carpophytes, Oöphytes, Protophytes, and Zygophytes (or Carposporeæ, Oösporeæ, Protophyta, and Zygosporeæ) was proposed by Sachs about 1875.
cadmean: Of or pertaining to Cadmus, a fabulous prince of Thebes, who was said to have introduced into Greece the sixteen simple letters of the alphabet -- Cadmean letters. Cadmean victory, a victory that damages the victors as much as the vanquished; probably referring to the battle in which the soldiers who sprang from the dragon's teeth sown by Cadmus slew each other.
calabar: A district on the west coast of Africa. Calabar bean, The of a climbing legumious plant (Physostigma venenosum), a native of tropical Africa. It is highly poisonous. It is used to produce contraction of the pupil of the eye; also in tetanus, neuralgia, and rheumatic diseases; -- called also ordeal bean, being used by the negroes in trials for witchcraft.
cannelcoal: A kind of mineral coal of a black color, sufficiently hard and solid to be cut and polished. It burns readily, with a clear, yellow flame, and on this account has been used as a substitute for candles.
cautionaryblock: A block in which two or more trains are permitted to travel, under restrictions imposed by a caution card or the like.
carving: 1. The act or art of one who carves. 2. A piece of decorative work cut in stone, wood, or other material. "Carving in wood." Sir W. Temple. 3. The whole body of decorative sculpture of any kind or epoch, or in any material; as, the Italian carving of the 15th century.
cachaemia: A degenerated or poisoned condition of the blood. | A degenerated or poisoned condition of the blood. --Ca*chæ"mic, Ca*che"mic (#), a.
carborundumpaper: Cloth or paper covered with powdered carborundum.
cautioner: 1. One who cautions or advises. 2. (Scots Law) A surety or sponsor.
capsular: Of or pertaining to a capsule; having the nature of a capsula; hollow and fibrous. Capsular ligament (Anat.), a ligamentous bag or capsule surrounding many movable joints in the skeleton.
catchwork: A work or artificial watercourse for throwing water on lands that lie on the slopes of hills; a catchdrain.
catacaustic: Relating to, or having the properties of, a caustic curve formed by reflection. See Caustic, a. Nichol. | A caustic curve formed by reflection of light. Nichol.
caret: A mark [^] used by writers and proof readers to indicate that something is interlined above, or inserted in the margin, which belongs in the place marked by the caret. | The hawkbill turtle. See Hawkbill.
cancrine: Having the qualities of a crab; crablike.
cadrans: An instrument with a graduated disk by means of which the angles of gems are measured in the process of cutting and polishing.
capsize: To upset or overturn, as a vessel or other body. But what if carrying sail capsize the boat Byron.
cassepaper: Broken paper; the outside quires of a ream.
carotte: A cylindrical roll of tobacco; as, a carotte of perique.
capacious: 1. Having capacity; able to contain much; large; roomy; spacious; extended; broad; as, a capacious vessel, room, bay, or harbor. In the capacious recesses of his mind. Bancroft. 2. Able or qualified to make large views of things, as in obtaining knowledge or forming designs; comprehensive; liberal. "A capacious mind." Watts.
caress: An act of endearment; any act or expression of affection; an embracing, or touching, with tenderness. Wooed her with his soft caresses. Langfellow. He exerted himself to win by indulgence and… | To treat with tokens of fondness, affection, or kindness; to touch or speak to in a loving or endearing manner; to fondle. The lady caresses the rough bloodhoun. Sir W. Scott. Syn. -- To foundle;
cahincic: Pertaining to, or derived from, cahinca, the native name of a species of Brazilian Chiococca, perhaps C. recemosa; as, cahincic acid.
carrying: The act or business of transporting from one place to another. Carrying place, a carry; a portage. -- Carrying trade, the business of transporting goods, etc., from one place or country to another by water or land; freighting. We are rivals with them in . . . the carrying trade. Jay.
carousing: That carouses; relating to a carouse.
calcific: Calciferous. Specifically: (Zoöl.) of or pertaining to hte portion of the which forms the eggshell in birds and reptiles. Huxley.
cauterization: The act of searing some morbid part by the application of a cautery or caustic; also, the effect of such application.
cabalistic: Of or pertaining to the cabala; containing or conveying an occult meaning; mystic. The Heptarchus is a cabalistic of the first chapter of Genesis. Hallam.
cathode: The part of a voltaic battery by which the electric current leaves substances through which it passes, or the surface at which the electric current passes out of the electrolyte; the negative pole; -- opposed to anode. Faraday. Cathode ray (Phys.), a kind of ray generated at the cathode in a vacuum tube, by the electrical discharge.
catilinarian: Pertaining to Catiline, the Roman conspirator; resembling Catiline's conspiracy.
capnomor: A limpid, colorless oil with a peculiar odor, obtained from beech tar. Watts.
camelbacked: Having a back like a camel; humpbacked. Fuller.
carnosity: 1. (Med.) A fleshy excrescence; esp. a small excrescence or fungous growth. Wiseman. 2. Fleshy substance or quality; fleshy covering. [Consciences] overgrown with so hard a carnosity. Spelman. The olives, indeed be very small there, and bigger than capers; yet commended they are for their carnosity. Holland. CARNOT'S CYCLE Car`not's" cy"cle. [After N. L. S.
caftan: A garment worn throughout the Levant, consisting of a long gown with sleeves reaching below the hands. It is generally fastened by a belt or sash. | To clothe with a caftan. The turbaned and caftaned damsel. Sir W. Scott.
castalian: Of or pertaining to Castalia, a mythical fountain of inspiration on Mt. Parnassus sacred to the Muses. Milton.
cassimere: A thin, twilled, woolen cloth, used for men's garments. [Written also kerseymere.]
cartequarte: A position in thrusting or parrying, with the inside of the hand turned upward and the point of the weapon toward the adversary's right breast.
caperer: One who capers, leaps, and skips about, or dances. The nimble capperer on the cord. Dryden.
cata: The Latin and English form of a Greek preposition, used as a prefix to signify down, downward, under, against, contrary or opposed to, wholly, completely; as in cataclysm, catarrh. It sometimes drops the final vowel, as in catoptric; and is sometimes changed to cath, as in cathartic, catholic.
catechetically: In a catechetical manner; by question and answer.
cannibal: A human being that eats human flesh; hence, any that devours its own kind. Darwin. | Relating to cannibals or cannibalism. "Cannibal terror." Burke.
carvelbuilt: Having the planks meet flush at the seams, instead of lapping as in a clinker-built vessel.
cabal: 1. Tradition; occult doctrine. See Cabala (old) Hakewill. 2. A secret. (old) "The measuring of the temple, a cabal found out but lately." B. Jonson. 3. A number of persons united in some close… | To unite in a small party to promote private views and interests by intrigue; to intrigue; to plot. Caballing still against it with the great. Dryden.
caltrop: 1. (Bot.) A genus of herbaceous plants (Tribulus) of the order Zygophylleæ, having a hard several-celled fruit, armed with stout spines, and resembling the military instrument of the same name. The species grow in warm countries, and are often very annoying to cattle. 2.
caira: The refrain of a famous song of the French Revolution.
cappeline: A hood-shaped bandage for the head, the shoulder, or the stump of an amputated limb.
caudad: Backwards; toward the tail or posterior part.
canaster: A kind of tobacco for smoking, made of the dried leaves, coarsely broken; -- so called from the rush baskets in which it is packed in South America. McElrath.
calcar: A kind of oven, or reverberatory furnace, used for the calcination of sand and potash, and converting them into frit. Ure. | 1. (Bot.) A hollow tube or spur at the base of a petal or corolla. 2. (Zoöl.) A slender bony process from the ankle joint of bats, which helps to support the posterior part of the web, in flight. 3.
cadene: A species of inferior carpet imported from the Levant. McElrath.
canaanite: 1. A descendant of Canaan, the son of Ham, and grandson of Noah. 2. A Native or inbabitant of the land of Canaan, esp. a member of any of the tribes who inhabited Canaan at the time of the exodus of… | A zealot. "Simon the Canaanite." Matt. x. 4. Note: This was the "Simon called Zelotes" (Luke vi. 15), i.e., Simon the zealot. Kitto.
capitular: 1. An act passed in a chapter. 2. A member of a chapter. The chapter itself, and all its members or capitulars. Ayliffe. 3. The head or prominent part. | 1. (Eccl.) Of or pertaining to a chapter; capitulary. From the pope to the member of the capitular body. Milman. 2. (Bot.) Growing in, or pertaining to, a capitulum. 3.
casein: A proteid substance present in both the animal and the vegetable kingdom. In the animal kindom it is chiefly found in milk, and constitutes the main part of the curd separated by rennet; in the vegetable kingdom it is found more or less abundantly in the seeds of leguminous plants. Its reactions resemble those of alkali albumin. [Written also caseine.]
carbineer: A soldier armed with a carbine.
catstitch: To fold and sew down the edge of with a coarse zigzag stitch.
cambrasine: A kind of linen cloth made in Egypt, and so named from its resemblance to cambric.
canonbit: That part of a bit which is put in a horse's mouth.
cambria: The ancient Latin name of Wales. It is used by modern poets.
cachiri: A fermented liquor made in Cayenne from the grated root of the manioc, and resembling perry. Dunglison.
candlepin: (a) A form of pin slender and nearly straight like a candle. (b) The game played with such pins; -- in form candlepins, used as a singular.
catchpenny: Made or contrived for getting small sums of money from the ignorant or unwary; as, a catchpenny book; a catchpenny show. -- n. Some worthless catchpenny thing.
cavorilievo: Hollow relief; sculpture in relief within a sinking made for the purpose, so no part of it projects beyond the plain surface around.
caladium: A genus of aroideous plants, of which some species are cultivated for their immense leaves (which are often curiously blotched with white and red), and others (in Polynesia) for food.
calendrical: Of or pertaining to a calendar.
cacodyl: Alkarsin; a colorless, poisonous, arsenical liquid, As2(CH3)4, spontaneously inflammable and possessing an intensely disagreeable odor. It is the type of a series of compounds analogous to the nitrogen compounds called hydrazines. [Written also cacodyle, and kakodyl.]
caution: 1. A careful attention to the probable effects of an act, in order that failure or harm may be avoided; prudence in regard to danger; provident care; wariness. 2. Security; guaranty; bail. | To give notice of danger to; to warn; to exhort [one] to take heed. You cautioned me against their charms. Swift.
catelectrode: The negative electrode or pole of a voltaic battery. Faraday.
campanulaceous: Of pertaining to, or resembling, the family of plants (Camponulaceæ) of which Campanula is the type, and which includes the Canterbury bell, the harebell, and the Venus's looking-glass.
cachinnation: Loud or immoderate laughter; -- often a symptom of hysterical or maniacal affections. Hideous grimaces . . . attended this unusual cachinnation. Sir W. Scott.
cavatina: Originally, a melody of simpler form than the aria; a song without a second part and a da capo; -- a term now variously and vaguely used.
cavalero: A cavalier; a gallant; a libertine. Shak.
calandine: A perennial herbaceous plant (Chelidonium majus) of the poppy family, with yellow flowers. It is used as a medicine in jandice, etc., and its acrid saffron-colored juice is used to cure warts and the itch; -- called also greater celandine and swallowwort. Lasser celandine, the pilewort (Ranunculus Ficaria).
calcareous: Partaking of the nature ofcalcite or calcium carbonate; consisting of, or containg, calcium carbonate or carbonate of lime. Clcareous spar. See as Calcite.
cachectical: Having, or pertaining to, cachexia; as, cachectic remedies; cachectical blood. Arbuthnot.
catechist: One who instructs by question and answer, especially in religions matters.
cacoethes: 1. A bad custom or habit; an insatiable desire; as, cacoëthes scribendi, "The itch for writing". Addison. 2. (Med.) A bad quality or disposition in a disease; an incurable ulcer.
carbonprocess: A printing process depending on the effect of light on bichromatized gelatin. Paper coated with a mixture of the gelatin and a pigment is called carbon paper or carbon tissue. This is exposed under a negative and the film is transferred from the paper to some other support and developed by washing (the unexposed portions being dissolved away).
calcography: The art of drawing with chalk.
caducity: Tendency to fall; the feebleness of old age; senility. [A] jumble of youth and caducity. Chesterfield.
cawky: Of or pertaining to cawk; like cawk.
calmucks: ; sing. Calmuck. A branch of the Mongolian race inbabiting parts of the Russian and Chinese empires; also (sing.), the language of the Calmucks. [Written also Kalmucks.]
casal: Of or pertaining to case; as, a casal ending.
capillaceous: Having long filaments; resembling a hair; slender. See Capillary.
catfall: A rope used in hoisting the anchor to the cathead. Totten.
caseworm: A worm or grub that makes for itself a case. See Caddice.
calyculate: Having a set of bracts resembling a calyx.
camisated: Dressed with a shirt over the other garments.
capellet: A swelling, like a wen, on the point of the elbow (or the heel of the hock) of a horse, caused probably by bruises in lying dowm.
capelin: A small marine fish (Mallotus villosus) of the family Salmonidæ, very abundant on the coasts of Greenland, Iceland, Newfoundland, and Alaska. It is used as a bait for the cod. [Written also capelan and caplin.] Note: This fish, which is like a smelt, is called by the Spaniards anchova, and by the Portuguese capelina. Fisheries of U. S. (1884).
cacaine: The essential principle of cacao; -- now called theobromine.
carousal: A jovial feast or festival; a drunken revel; a carouse. The swains were preparing for a carousal. Sterne. Syn. -- Banquet; revel; orgie; carouse. See Feast.
caudle: A kind of warm drink for sick persons, being a mixture of wine with eggs, bread, sugar, and spices. | 1. To make into caudle. 2. Too serve as a caudle to; to refresh. Shak.
campanology: The art of ringing bells, or a treatise on the art.
cantoon: A cotton stuff showing a fine cord on one side and a satiny surface on the other.
capsulated: Inclosed in a capsule, or as in a chest or box.
cassock: 1. A long outer garment formerly worn by men and women, as well as by soldiers as part of their uniform. 2. (Eccl.) A garment resembling a long frock coat worn by the clergy of certain churches when officiating, and by others as the usually outer garment.
capsulate: Inclosed in a capsule, or as in a chest or box.
calceated: Fitted with, or wearing, shoes. Johnson.
calamary: A cephalopod, belonging to the genus Loligo and related genera. There are many species. They have a sack of inklike fluid which they discharge from the siphon tube, when pursued or alarmed, in order to confuse their enemies. Their shell is a thin horny plate, within the flesh of back, shaped very much like a quill pen. In America they are called squids. See Squid.
carpintero: A california woodpecker (Melanerpes formicivorus), noted for its habit of inserting acorns in holes which it drills in trees. The acorns become infested by insect larvæ, which, when grown, are extracted for food by the bird.
capitate: 1. Headlike in form; also, having the distal end enlarged and rounded, as the stigmas of certain flowers. 2. (Bot.) Having the flowers gathered into a head.
caprification: The practice of hanging, upon the cultivated fig tree, branches of the wild fig infested with minute hymenopterous insects. Note: It is supposed that the little insects insure fertilization by carrying the pollen from the male flowers near the opening of the fig down to the female flowers, and also accelerate ripening the fruit by puncturing it.
caliber: 1. (Gunnery) The diameter of the bore, as a cannon or other firearm, or of any tube; or the weight or size of the projectile which a firearm will carry; as, an 8 inch gun, a 12-pounder, a 44 caliber. The caliber of empty tubes. Reid. A battery composed of three guns of small caliber. Prescott. Note: The caliber of firearms is expressed in various ways.
calyon: Flint or pebble stone, used in building walls, etc. Haliwell.
caries: Ulceration of bone; a process in which bone disintegrates and is carried away piecemeal, as distinguished from necrosis, in which it dies in masses.
calyptriform: Having the form a calyptra, or extinguisher.
campaign: 1. An open field; a large, open plain without considerable hills. SeeChampaign. Grath. 2. (Mil.) A connected series of military operations forming a distinct stage in a war; the time during which an army keeps the field. Wilhelm. 3. Political operations preceding an election; a canvass. [Cant, U. S.] 4.
camaraderie: Comradeship and loyalty. The spirit of camaraderie is strong among these riders of the plains. W. A. Fraser.
cataian: A native of Cathay or China; a foreigner; -- formerly a term of reproach. Shak.
cadillac: A large pear, shaped like a flattened top, used chiefly for cooking. Johnson.
cauter: A hot iron for searing or cauterizing. Minsheu.
captivate: 1. To take prisoner; to capture; to subdue. (old) Their woes whom fortune captivates. Shak. 2. To acquire ascendancy over by reason of some art or attraction; to fascinate; to charm; | Taken prisoner; made captive; insnared; charmed. Women have been captivate ere now. Shak.
cautelous: 1. Caution; prudent; wary. (old) "Cautelous, though young." Drayton. 2. Crafty; deceitful; false. (old) Shak. -- Cau"te*lous*ly, adv. -- Cau"te*lous*ness, n. (old)
capricorn: 1. (Astron.) The tenth sign of zodiac, into which the sun enters at the winter solstice, about December 21. See Tropic. The sun was entered into Capricorn. Dryden. 2. (Astron.) A southern constellation, represented on ancient monuments by the figure of a goat, or a figure with its fore part like a fish. Capricorn beetle (Zoöl.), any beetle of the family Carambucidæ;
came: A slender rod of cast lead, with or without grooves, used, in casements and stained-glass windows, to hold together the panes or pieces of glass.
calker: 1. One who calks. 2. A calk on a shoe. See Calk, n., 1.
carbonarism: The principles, practices, or organization of the Carbonari.
carthamin: A red coloring matter obtained from the safflower, or Carthamus tinctorius.
calcarine: Pertaining to, or situated near, the calcar of the brain.
caduke: Perishable; frail; transitory. (old) Hickes. The caduke pleasures of his world. Bp. Fisher.
candlestick: An instrument or utensil for supporting a candle.
candidacy: The position of a candidate; state of being a candidate; candidateship.
cancan: A rollicking French dance, accompanied by indecorous or extravagant postures and gestures.
career: 1. A race course: the ground run over. To go back again the same career. Sir P. Sidney. 2. A running; full speed; a rapid course. When a horse is running in his full career. Wilkins. 3. | To move or run rapidly. areering gayly over the curling waves. W. Irving.
calibration: The process of estimating the caliber a tube, as of a thermometer tube, in order to graduate it to a scale of degrees; also, more generally, the determination of the true value of the spaces in any graduated instrument.
card: 1. A piece of pasteboard, or thick paper, blank or prepared for various uses; as, a playing card; a visiting card; a card of invitation; pl. a game played with cards. | To play at cards; to game. Johnson.
car: 1. A small vehicle moved on wheels; usually, one having but two wheels and drawn by one horse; a cart. 2. A vehicle adapted to the rails of a railroad. [U. S.] Note: In England a railroad passenger car is called a railway carriage; a freight car a goods wagon; a platform car a goods truck; a baggage car a van.
casually: Without design; accidentally; fortuitously; by chance; occasionally.
cachucha: An Andalusian dance in three-four time, resembing the bolero. [Sometimes in English spelled cachuca (.] The orchestra plays the cachucha. Logfellow.
caruncle: 1. (Anat.) A small fleshy prominence or excrescence; especially the small, reddish body, the caruncula lacrymalis, in the inner angle of the eye. 2. (Bot.) An excrescence or appendage surrounding or near the hilum of a seed. 3. (Zoöl.) A naked, flesh appendage, on the head of a bird, as the wattles of a turkey, etc.
calotte: A close cap without visor or brim. Especially: (a) Such a cap, worn by English serjeants at law. (b) Such a cap, worn by the French cavalry under their helmets. (c) Such a cap, worn by the clergy of the Roman Catholic Church. To assume the calotte, to become a priest.
capitularly: In the manner or form of an ecclesiastical chapter. Sterne.
cardinalize: To exalt to the office of a cardinal. Sheldon.
capella: A brilliant star in the constellation Auriga.
cayenne: Cayenne pepper. Cayenne pepper. (a) (Bot.) A species of capsicum (C. frutescens) with small and intensely pungent fruit. (b) A very pungent spice made by drying and grinding the fruits or seeds of several species of the genus Capsicum, esp. C. annuum and C. Frutescens; -- Called also red pepper. It is used chiefly as a condiment.
cannabin: A pisonous resin extracted from hemp (Cannabis sativa, variety Indica). The narcotic effects of hasheesh are due to this resin.
carrageen: A small, purplish, branching, cartilaginous seaweed (Chondrus crispus), which, when bleached, is the Irish moss of commerce. [Also written carragheen, carageen.]
carpentering: The occupation or work of a carpenter; the act of workingin timber; carpentry.
capper: 1. One whose business is to make or sell caps. 2. A by-bidder; a decoy for gamblers [Slang, U. S.]. 3. An instrument for applying a percussion cap to a gun or cartridge.
catchmeadow: meadow irrigated by water from a spring or rivulet on the side of hill.
carbon: An elementary substance, not metallic in its nature, which is present in all organic compounds. Atomic weight 11.97. Symbol C. it is combustible, and forms the base of lampblack and charcoal, and enters largely into mineral coals.
caravansary: A kind of inn, in the East, where caravans rest at night, being a large, rude, unfurnished building, surrounding a court. [Written also caravanserai and caravansera.]
castoreum: A peculiar bitter orange-brown substance, with strong, penetrating odor, found in two sacs between the anus and external genitals of the beaver; castor; -- used in medicine as an antispasmodic, and by perfumers.
carmileage: (a) Car miles collectively. (b) The amount paid by one road the use of cars of another road.
caffeine: A white, bitter, crystallizable substance, obtained from coffee. It is identical with the alkaloid theine from tea leaves, and with guaranine from guarana.
catchtitle: A short expressive title used for abbreviated book lists, etc.
carminated: Of, relating to, or mixed with, carmine; as, carminated lake. Tomlinson.
casemate: 1. (Fort.) A bombproof chamber, usually of masonry, in which cannon may be placed, to be fired through embrasures; or one capable of being used as a magazine, or for quartering troops. 2. (Arch.) A hollow molding, chiefly in cornices.
cascarilla: A euphorbiaceous West Indian shrub (Croton Eleutheria); also, its aromatic bark. Cascarilla bark (or Cascarila) (Med.), the bark of Croton Eleutheria. It has an aromatic odor and a warm, spicy, bitter taste, and when burnt emits a musky odor.
canker: 1. A corroding or sloughing ulcer; esp. a spreading gangrenous ulcer or collection of ulcers in or about the mouth; -- called also water canker, canker of the mouth, and noma. 2. | 1. To affect as a canker; to eat away; to corrode; to consune. No lapse of moons can canker Love. Tennyson. 2. To infect or pollute; to corrupt. Addison. A tithe purloined canker the whole estate.
carman: A man whose employment is to drive, or to convey goods in, a car or car.
camonflet: A small mine, sometimes formed in the wall or side of an enemy's gallery, to blow in the earth and cut off the retreat of the miners. Farrow.
camoys: Flat; depressed; crooked; -- said only of the nose. (old)
carping: Fault-finding; censorious caviling. See Captious. -- Carp"ing*ly, adv.
caloric: The principle of heat, or the agent to which the phenomena of heat and combustion were formerly ascribed; -- not now used in scientific nomenclature, but sometimes used as a general term for heat. | Of or pertaining to caloric. Caloric engine, a kind of engine operated air.
carpogenic: Productive of fruit, or causing fruit to be developed.
caponiere: A work made across or in the ditch, to protect it from the enemy, or to serve as a covered passageway.
cantaloupe: A muskmelon of several varieties, having when mature, a yellowish skin, and flesh of a reddish orange color. [Written also cantaleup.]
catchy: 1. Apt or tending to catch the fancy or attention; catching; taking; as, catchy music. 2. Tending to catch or insnare; entangling; -- usually used fig.; as, a catchy question. 3. Consisting of, or occuring in, disconnected parts or snatches; changeable; as, a catchy wind. It [the fox's scent] is . . . flighty or catchy, if variable. Encyc. of Sport.
camellia: An Asiatic genus of small shrubs, often with shining leaves and showy flowers. Camelia Japonica is much cultivated for ornament, and C. Sassanqua and C. Oleifera are grown in China for the oil which is pressed from their seeds. The tea plant is now referred to this genus under the name of Camellia Thea.
candify: To make or become white, or candied.
camerlingo: The papal chamberlain; the cardinal who presides over the pope's household. He has at times possessed great power. [Written also camerlengo and camarlengo.]
catechetics: The science or practice of instructing by questions and answers.
caseknife: 1. A knife carried in a sheath or case. Addison. 2. A large table knife; -- so called from being formerly kept in a case.
catadromous: 1. (Bot.) Having the lowest inferior segment of a pinna nearer the rachis than the lowest superior one; -- said of a mode of branching in ferns, and opposed to anadromous. 2. (Zoöl.) Living in fresh water, and going to the sea to spawn; -- opposed to anadromous, and of the eel.
calligraphic: Of or pertaining to calligraphy. Excellence in the calligraphic act. T. Warton.
carom: A shot in which the ball struck with the cue comes in contact with two or more balls on the table; a hitting of two or more balls with the player's ball. In England it is called cannon.
calvaria: The bones of the cranium; more especially, the bones of the domelike upper portion.
cardiogram: The curve or tracing made by a cardiograph.
cartoon: 1. A design or study drawn of the full size, to serve as a model for transferring or copying; -- used in the making of mosaics, tapestries, fresco pantings and the like; as, the cartoons of Raphael. 2. A large pictorial sketch, as in a journal or magazine; esp. a pictorial caricature; as , the cartoons of "Puck."
camphor: 1. A tough, white, aromatic resin, or gum, obtained from different species of the Laurus family, esp. from Cinnamomum camphara (the Laurus camphara of Linnæus.). Camphor, C10H16O, is volatile and… | To impregnate or wash with camphor; to camphorate. Tatler.
carbonaro: A member of a secret political association in Italy, organized in the early part of the nineteenth centry for the purpose of changing the government into a republic. Note: The origin of the Carbonari is uncertain, but the society is said to have first met, in 1808, among the charcoal burners of the mountains, whose phraseology they adopted.
cascarillin: A white, crystallizable, bitter substance extracted from oil of cascarilla.
cavendish: Leaf tobacco softened, sweetened, and pressed into plugs or cakes. Cut cavendish, the plugs cut into long shreds for smoking.
caricature: 1. An exaggeration, or distortion by exaggeration, of parts or characteristics, as in a picture. 2. A picture or other figure or description in which the peculiarities of a person or thing are so… | To make or draw a caricature of; to represent with ridiculous exaggeration; to burlesque. He could draw an ill face, or caricature a good one, with a masterly hand. Lord Lyttelton.

cavaliero: A cavalier; a gallant; a libertine. Shak.

caecilian: A limbless amphibian belonging to the order Cæciliæ or Ophimorpha. See Ophiomorpha. [Written also coecilian.]
catamenial: Pertaining to the catamenia, or menstrual discharges.
caroched: Placed in a caroche. (old) Beggary rides caroched. Massenger.
calendulin: A gummy or mucilaginous tasteless substance obtained from the marigold or calendula, and analogous to bassorin.
catelectrotonic: Relating to, or characterized by, catelectrotonus.
catadioptric: Pertaining to, produced by, or involving, both the reflection and refraction of light; as, a catadioptric light. Hutton.
cazique: A chief or petty king among some tribes of Indians in America.
casuistical: Of or pertaining to casuists or casuistry.

carneous: Consisting of, or like, flesh; carnous; fleshy. "Carneous fibers." Ray.

cantabrian: Of or pertaining to Cantabria on the Bay of Biscay in Spain.
catallactics: The science of exchanges, a branch of political economy.
caption: 1. A caviling; a sophism. (old) This doctrine is for caption and contradiction. Bacon. 2. The act of taking or arresting a person by judicial process. Bouvier. 3. capote: A long cloak or overcoat, especially one with a hood.
canvass: 1. calcinable: That may be calcined; as, a calcinable fossil.
cankerfly: A fly that preys on fruit.

carnauba: The Brazilian wax palm. See Wax palm.
cappingplane: A plane used for working the upper surface of staircase rails.

cavally: A carangoid fish of the Atlantic coast (Caranx hippos): -- called also horse crevallé. Note: [See Illust. under Carangoid.]

canteen: 1. A vessel used by soldiers for carrying water, liquor, or other drink. cataphonics: That branch of acoustics which treats of reflested sounds; catacoustics.
causer: One who or that which causes.
canoe: 1. A boat used by rude nations, formed of trunk of a tree, excavated, by cutting of burning, into a suitable shape. It is propelled by a paddle or paddles, or sometimes by sail, and has no rudder. | To manage a canoe, or voyage in a canoe.

catoptrics: That part of optics which explants the properties and phenomena of reflected light, and particularly that which is reflected from mirrors or polished bodies; --- formerly caled anacamptics.
cavitary: Containing a body cavity; as, the cavitary or nematoid worms.
carabid: Of, pertaining to, or resembling, the genus Carbus or family Carabidæ. -- n. One of the Carabidæ, a family of active insectivorous beetles.
cassava: 1. (Bot.) A shrubby euphorbiaceous plant of the genus Manihot, with fleshy rootstocks yielding an edible starch; -- called also manioc. cardoon: A large herbaceos plant (Cynara Cardunculus) related to the artichoke; -- used in cookery and as a sald.
calf: 1. The young of the cow, or of the Bovine family of quadrupeds. Also, the young of some other mammals, as of the elephant, rhinoceros, hippopotamus, and whale. 2. carriage: 1. That which is carried; burden; baggage. (old) David left his carriage in the hand of the keeper of the carriage. 1. Sam. xvii. 22. capableness: The quality or state of being capable; capability; adequateness; competency.
cascalho: A deposit of pebbles, gravel, and ferruginous sand, in which the Brazilian diamond is usually found.

catlinite: A red clay from the Upper Missouri region, used by the Indians for their pipes.

careenage: (a) Expense of careening ships. (b) A place for careening.

cardamom: 1. The aromatic fruit, or capsule with its seeds, of several plants of the Ginger family growing in the East Indies and elsewhere, and much used as a condiment, and in medicine. 2. (Bot.) A plant which prduces cardamoms, esp. Elettaria Cardamomum and several of Amommum.

cataphonic: Of or relating to cataphonics; catacoustic.

calculable: That may be calculated or ascertained by calculation.

caraboid: Like, or pertaining to the genus Carabus.
caledonite: A hydrous sulphate of copper and lead, found in some parts of Caledonia or Scotland.
calin: An alloy of lead and tin, of which the Chinese make tea canisters.
calefactor: A heater; one who, or that which, makes hot, as a stove, etc.
cabotage: Navigation along the coast; the details of coast pilotage.

capnomancy: Divination by means of the ascent or motion of smoke.
cardioid: An algebraic curve, so called from its resemblance to a heart.
carthusian: A member of an exceeding austere religious order, founded at Chartreuse in France by St. Bruno, in the year 1086.
caldron: A large kettle or boiler of copper, brass, or iron. [Written also cauldron.] "Caldrons of boiling oil." Prescott.
cardialgla: A burning or gnawing pain, or feeling of distress, referred to the region of the heart, accompanied with cardisc palpitation; heartburn. It is usually a symptom of indigestion.
caesar: A Roman emperor, as being the successor of Augustus Cæsar. Hence, a kaiser, or emperor of Germany, or any emperor or powerful ruler. See Kaiser, Kesar. cacography: Incorrect or bad writing or spelling. Walpole.
caged: Confined in, or as in, a cage; like a cage or prison. "The caged cloister." Shak.

cankery: 1. Like a canker; full of canker. 2. Surly; sore; malignant.
carpolite: A general term for a fossil fruit, nut, or seed.
calmly: In a calm manner. The gentle stream which calmly flows. Denham.
caroline: A silver coin once current in some parts of Italy, worth about seven cents. Simmonds.
calle: A kind of head covering; a caul. (old) Chaucer.
caple: A horse; a nag. (old) Chaucer. Holland.

candiot: Of or pertaining to Candia; Cretary.

carnalism: The state of being carnal; carnality; sensualism.
carelessness: The quality or state of being careless; heedlessness; negligenece; inattention.
capitellate: Having a very small knoblike termination, or collected into minute capitula.
cabala: 1. A kind of occult theosophy or traditional interpretation of the Scriptures among Jewish rabbis and certain mediæval Christians, which treats of the nature of god and the mystery of human existence. caimacam: The governor of a sanjak or district in Turkey.

caada: A small cañon; a narrow valley or glen; also, but less frequently, an open valley. [Local, Western U. S.]
campestral: Relating to an open fields; drowing in a field; growing in a field, or open ground.
camphene: One of a series of substances C10H16, resembling camphor, regarded as modified terpenes.
caducibranchiate: With temporary gills: -- applied to those Amphibia in which the gills do not remain in adult life.

cassonade: Raw sugar; sugar not refined. Mc Elrath.

cauf: A chest with holes for keeping fish alive in water. Philips.
carton: Pasteboard for paper boxes; also, a pasteboard box. Carton pierre (, a species of papier-maché, imitating stone or bronze sculpture. Knight.
caboched: Showing the full face, but nothing of the neck; -- said of the head of a beast in armorial bearing. [Written also caboshed.]
canicular: Pertaining to, or measured, by the rising of the Dog Star. Canicular days, the dog days, See Dog days. -- Canicular year, the Egyptian year, computed from one heliacal rising of the Dog Star to another.
cacodemon: 1. An evil spirit; a devil or demon. Shak. 2. (Med.) The nightmare. Dunaglison.
calendric: Of or pertaining to a calendar.
causality: 1. The agency of a cause; the action or power of a cause, in producing its effect. The causality of the divine mind. Whewell. 2. (Phren.) The faculty of tracing effects to their causes. G. Combe.
capitatim: Of so much per head; as, a capitatim tax; a capitatim grant.

caudicula: A slender, elastic process, to which the masses of pollen in orchidaceous plants are attached.
castellan: A goveror or warden of a castle.

carex: A numerous and widely distributed genus of perennial herbaceous plants of the order Cypreaceæ; the sedges.
caecias: A wind from the northeast. Milton.
caoutchin: An inflammable, volatile, oily, liquid hydrocarbon, obtained by the destructive distillation of caoutchouc.
catapeltic: Of or pertaining to a catapult.
cageling: A bird confined in a cage; esp. a young bird. (poetic) Tennyson.
carbohydrate: One of a group of compounds including the sugars, starches, and gums, which contain six (or some multiple of six) carbon atoms, united with a variable number of hydrogen and oxygen atoms, but with the two latter always in proportion as to form water; as dextrose, C6H12O6.
carlovingian: Pertaining to, founded by, of descended from, Charlemagne; as, the Carlovingian race of kings.
canticle: 1. A song; esp. a little song or hymn. (old) Bacon. 2. pl. The Song of Songs or Song of Solomon, one of the books of the Old Testament. 3. A canto or division of a poem (old) Spenser. 4. A psalm, hymn, or passage from the Bible, arranged for chanting in church service.

cauliform: Having the form of a caulis.
calumniator: One who calumniates. Syn. -- Slanderer; defamer; libeler; traducer.

canty: Cheerful; sprightly; lively; merry. "The canty dame." Wordsworth [Scot. & Prov. Eng.] Contented with little, and canty with mair. Burns.

canaliculate: Having a channel or groove, as in the leafstalks of most palms.
casuistry: 1. casebay: (a) The space between two principals or girders. (b) One of the joists framed between a pair of girders in naked flooring.
catechismal: Of or pertaining to a catechism, having the form of questions and answers; catechical.
cadmic: Pertaining to, derived from, or containing, cadmium; as, cadmic sulphide.

calcaneum: One of the bones of the tarsus which in man, forms the great bone of the heel; -- called also fibulare.

calycine: Pertaining to a calyx; having the nature of a calyx.

cadaster: An official statement of the quantity and value of real estate for the purpose of apportioning the taxes payable on such property.

capri: Wine produced on the island of Capri, commonly a light, dry, white wine.
castilian: 1. An inhabitant or native of Castile, in Spain. 2. The Spanish language as spoken in Castile.

catanadromous: Ascending and descending fresh streams from and to the sea, as the salmon; anadromous.
candor: 1. Whiteness; brightness; (as applied to moral conditions) usullied purity; innocence. cataplasm: A soft and moist substance applied externally to some part of the body; a poultice. Dunglison.

cadmia: An oxide of zinc which collects on the sides of furnaces where zinc is sublimed. Formerly applied to the mineral calamine.

cardamine: A genus of cruciferous plants, containing the lady's-smock, cuckooflower, bitter cress, meadow cress, etc.
candlelight: The light of a candle. Never went by candlelight to bed. Dryden.

canakin: A little can or cup. "And let me the canakin clink." Shak.
cantrip: A charm; an incantation; a shell; a trick; adroit mischief. [Written also cantraip.] [Scot.]
cackler: 1. A fowl that cackles. 2. One who prattles, or tells tales; a tattler.

calcareobituminous: Consisting of, or containing, lime and bitumen. Lyell.
carrigeen: A small, purplish, branching, cartilaginous seaweed (Chondrus crispus), which, when bleached, is the Irish moss of commerce. [Also written carragheen, carageen.]
catalogue: A list or enumeration of names, or articles arranged methodically, often in alphabetical order; as, a catalogue of the students of a college, or of books, or of the stars. | To make a list or catalogue; to insert in a catalogue.
cabaret: A tavern; a house where liquors are retailed. [Obs. as an English word.]
captain: 1. A head, or chief officer; as: (a) The military officer who commands a company, troop, or battery, or who has the rank entitling him to do so though he may be employed on other service. | To act as captain of; to lead. Men who captained or accompanied the exodus from existing forms. Lowell.
captious: 1. Art to catch at faults; disposed to find fault or to cavil; eager to object; difficult to please. A captius and suspicious. Stillingfleet. I am sensible I have not disposed my materials to adbide the test of a captious controversy. Bwike. 2. Fitted to harass, perplex, or insnare; insidious; troublesome. Captious restraints on navigation. Bancroft. Syn.
cantarro: 1. A weight used in southern Europe and East for heavy articles. It varies in different localities; thus, at Rome it is nearly 75 pounds, in Sardinia nearly 94 pounds, in Cairo it is 95 pounds, in Syria about 503 pounds. 2. A liquid measure in Spain, ranging from two and a half to four gallons. Simmonds.
catholic: 1. Universal or general; as, the catholic faith. Men of other countries [came] to bear their part in so great and catholic a war. Southey. Note: This epithet, which is applicable to the whole… | 1. A person who accepts the creeds which are received in common by all parts of the orthodox Christian church. 2. An adherent of the Roman Catholic church; a Roman Catholic.
carroty: Like a carrot in color or in taste; -- an epithet given to reddish yellow hair, etc.
carnality: The state of being carnal; fleshly lust, or the indulgence of lust; grossness of mind. Because of the carnality of their hearts. Tillotson.
capitoline: Of or pertaining to the Capitol in Rome. "Capitolian Jove." Macaulay. Capitoline games (Antiq.), annual games instituted at Rome by Camillus, in honor of Jupter Capitolinus, on account of the preservation of the Capitol from the Gauls; when reinstituted by Domitian, arter a period of neglect, they were held every fifth year.
causticily: 1. The quality of being caustic; corrosiveness; as, the causticity of potash. 2. Severity of language; sarcasm; as, the causticity of a reply or remark.
catchweight: Without any additional weight; without being handicapped; as, to ride catchweight.
cajolement: The act of cajoling; the state of being cajoled; cajolery. Coleridge.
calorimeter: 1. (Physiol.) An apparatus for measuring the amount of heat contained in bodies or developed by some mechanical or chemical process, as friction, chemical combination, combustion, etc. 2. (Engineering) An apparatus for measuring the proportion of unevaporated water contained in steam.
callithump: A somewhat riotous parade, accompanied with the blowing of tin horus, and other discordant noises; also, a burlesque serenade; a charivari. [U. S.]
catling: 1. A little cat; a kitten. "Cat nor catling." Drummond. 2. Catgut; a catgut string. Shak. 3. (Surg.) A double-edged, sharp-pointed dismembering knife. [Spelt also catlin.] Crobb.
cankerworm: The larva of two species of geometrid moths which are very injurious to fruit and shade trees by eating, and often entirely destroying, the foliage. Other similar larvæ are also called cankerworms. Note: The autumnal species (Anisopteryx pometaria) becomes adult late in autumn (after frosts) and in winter. The spring species (A.
cacoxene: A hydrous phosphate of iron occurring in yellow radiated tufts. The phosphorus seriously injures it as an iron ore.
cavetto: A concave molding; -- used chiefly in classical architecture. See Illust. of Calumn.
canonistic: Of or pertaining to a canonist. "This canonistic exposition." Milton.
cashmerette: A kind of dress goods, made with a soft and glossy surface like cashmere.
caisson: 1. (Mil.) (a) A chest to hold ammunition. (b) A four-wheeled carriage for conveying ammunition, consisting of two parts, a body and a limber. In light field batteries there is one caisson to each piece, having two ammunition boxes on the body, and one on the limber. Farrow.
cariole: (a) A small, light, open one-horse carriage. (b) A covered cart. (c) A kind of calash. See Carryall.
capoc: A sort of cotton so short and fine thet it can not be spun, used in the East Indies to line palanquins, to make mattresses, etc.
cajun: In Louisiana, a person reputed to be Acadian French descent.
cacomixle: A North American carnivore (Bassaris astuta), about the size of a cat, related to the raccoons. It inhabits Mexico, Texas, and California.
cabochon: A stone of convex form, highly polished, but not faceted; also, the style of cutting itself. Such stones are said to be cut en cabochon.
cathodegraph: A picture produced by the Röntgen rays; a radiograph.
canterbury: 1. A city in England, giving its name various articles. It is the seat of the Archbishop of Canterbury (primate of all England), and contains the shrine of Thomas à Becket, to which pilgrimages were formerly made. 2. A stand with divisions in it for holding music, loose papers, etc.
cartogram: A map showing geographically, by shades or curves, statistics of various kinds; a statistical map.
carnify: To form flesh; to become like flesh. Sir M. Hale.
carven: Wrought by carving; ornamented by carvings; carved. (poetic) A carven bowl well wrought of beechen tree. Bp. Hall. The carven cedarn doors. Tennyson. A screen of carven ivory. Mrs. Browning.
cancroid: 1. (Zoöl.) Resembling a crab; pertaining to the Cancroidea, one of the families of crabs, including the genus Cancer. 2. Like a cancer; as, a cancroid tumor.
carriageable: Passable by carriages; that can be conveyed in carriages. Ruskin.
catenation: Connection of links or union of parts, as in a chain; a regular or connected series. See Concatenation. Sir T. Browne.
caber: A pole or beam used in Scottish games for tossing as a trial of strength.
cancerate: To grow into a canser; to become cancerous. Boyle.
castrametation: The art or act of encamping; the making or laying out of a camp.
caird: A traveling tinker; also a tramp or sturdy beggar. [Prov. Eng.]
carcinoma: A cancer. By some medical writers, the term is applied to an indolent tumor. See Cancer. Dunglison.
canoeing: The act or art of using a canoe.
calligraphical: Of or pertaining to calligraphy. Excellence in the calligraphic act. T. Warton.
caporal: One who directs work; an overseer. [Sp. Amer.]
camarilla: 1. The private audience chamber of a king. 2. A company of secret and irresponsible advisers, as of a king; a cabal or clique.
calk: 1. To drive tarred oakum into the seams between the planks of (a ship, boat, etc.), to prevent leaking. The calking is completed by smearing the seams with melted pitch. 2. | To copy, as a drawing, by rubbing the back of it with red or black chalk, and then passing a blunt style or needle over the lines, so as to leave a tracing on the paper or other thing against which…
catboat: A small sailboat, with a single mast placed as far forward as possible, carring a sail extended by a graff and long boom. See Illustration in Appendix.
campylospermous: Having seeds grooved lengthwise on the inner face, as in sweet cicely.
casting: 1. The act of one who casts or throws, as in fishing. 2. The act or process of making cast or impressions, or of shaping metal or plaster in a mold; the act or the process of pouring molten metal into a mold. 3. That which is cast in a mold; esp. the mass of metal so cast; as, a casting in iron; bronze casting. 4. The warping of a board. Brande & C. 5.
cardia: (a) The heart. (b) The anterior or cardiac orifice of the stomach, where the esophagus enters it.
calipash: A part of a turtle which is next to the upper shell. It contains a fatty and gelatinous substance of a dull greenish tinge, much esteemed as a delicacy in preparations of turtle.
case: 1. A box, sheath, or covering; as, a case for holding goods; a case for spectacles; the case of a watch; the case (capsule) of a cartridge; a case (cover) for a book. 2. A box and its contents; | 1. To cover or protect with, or as with, a case; to inclose. The man who, cased in steel, had passed whole days and nights in the saddle. Prescott. 2. To strip the skin from; as, to case a box. (old)
casa: A house or mansion. [Sp. Amer. & Phil. Islands] I saw that Enriquez had made no attempt to modernize the old casa, and that even the garden was left in its lawless native luxuriance. Bret Harte.
calcium: An elementary substance; a metal which combined with oxygen forms lime. It is of a pale yellow color, tenacious, and malleable. It is a member of the alkaline earth group of elements. Atomic weight 40. Symbol Ca.
canalization: Construction of, or furnishing with, a canal or canals.
canopus: A star of the first magnitude in the southern constellation Argo.
cavy: A rodent of the genera cavia and Dolichotis, as the guinea pig (Cavia cabaya). Cavies are natives of South America. Water cavy (Zoöl.), The capybara.
cavalcade: A procession of persons on horseback; a formal, pompous march of horsemen by way of parade. He brought back war-worn cavalcade to the city. Prescott.
capillation: A capillary blood vessel. (old) Sir T. Browne.
camphoraceous: Of the nature of camphor; containing camphor. Dunglison.
caviller: One who cavils. Cavilers at the style of the Scriptures. Boyle.
calipers: An instrument, usually resembling a pair of dividers or compasses with curved legs, for measuring the diameter or thickness of bodies, as of work shaped in a lathe or planer, timber, masts, shot, etc.; or the bore of firearms, tubes, etc.; -- called also caliper compasses, or caliber compasses.
calumet: A kind of pipe, used by the North American Indians for smoking tobacco. The bowl is usually made of soft red stone, and the tube is a long reed often ornamented with feathers. Smoked the calumet, the Peace pipe, As a signal to the nations. Lowgfellow. Note: The calumet is used as a symbol of peace.
carotic: 1. Of or pertaining to stupor; as, a carotic state. 2. (Anat.) Carotid; as, the carotic arteries.
carcajou: The wolverence; -- also applied, but erroneously, to the Canada lynx, and sometimes to the American badger. See Wolverene.
capsicine: A valatile alkaloid extracted from Capsicum annuum or from capsicin.
catenulate: 1. Consisting of little links or chains. 2. (Zoöl.) Chainlike; -- said both or color marks and of indentations when arranged like the links of a chain, as on shells, etc.
carcass: 1. A dead body, whether of man or beast; a corpse; now commonly the dead body of a beast. He turned to see the carcass of the lion. Judges xiv. 8. This kept thousands in the town whose carcasses went into the great pits by cartloads. De Foe. 2. The living body; -- now commonly used in contempt or ridicule. "To pamper his own carcass." South. Lovely her face;
calamar: A cephalopod, belonging to the genus Loligo and related genera. There are many species. They have a sack of inklike fluid which they discharge from the siphon tube, when pursued or alarmed, in order to confuse their enemies. Their shell is a thin horny plate, within the flesh of back, shaped very much like a quill pen. In America they are called squids. See Squid.
cavalierism: The practice or principles of cavaliers. Sir. W. Scott.
carwheel: A flanged wheel of a railway car or truck.
cadenza: A parenthetic flourish or flight of ornament in the course of a piece, commonly just before the final cadence.
calorescence: The conversion of obscure radiant heat info kight; the transmutation of rays of heat into others of higher refrangibility. Tyndall.
calade: A slope or declivity in a manege ground down which a horse is made to gallop, to give suppleness to his haunches.
carbonade: Flesh, fowl, etc., cut across, seasoned, and broiled on coals; a chop. (old) | 1. To cut (meat) across for frying or broiling; to cut or slice and broil. (old) A short-legged hen daintily carbonadoed. Bean. & Fl. 2. To cut or hack, as in fighting.
calmer: One who, or that which, makes calm.
caligo: Dimness or obscurity of sight, dependent upon a speck on the cornea; also, the speck itself.
cancellous: Having a spongy or porous stracture; made up of cancelli; cancellated; as, the cancellous texture of parts of many bones.
carronade: A kind of short cannon, formerly in use, designed to throw a large projectile with small velocity, used for the purpose of breaking or smashing in, rather than piercing, the object aimed at, as the side of a ship. It has no trunnions, but is supported on its carriage by a bolt passing through a loop on its under side.
carucage: 1. (Old Eng. Law.) A tax on every plow or plowland. 2. The act of plowing.
calvinism: The theological tenets or doctrines of John Calvin (a French theologian and reformer of the 16th century) and his followers, or of the so-called calvinistic churches.
caulis: An herbaceous or woody stem which bears leaves, and may bear flowers.
captation: A courting of favor or applause, by flattery or address; a captivating quality; an attraction. (old) Without any of those dresses, or popular captations, which some men use in their speeches. Eikon Basilike.
cartedevisite: 1. A visiting card. 2. A photographic picture of the size formerly in use for a visiting card.
cachinnatory: Consisting of, or accompanied by, immoderate laughter. Cachinnatory buzzes of approval. Carlyle.
carillon: 1. (Mus.) A chime of bells diatonically tuned, played by clockwork or by finger keys. 2. A tune adapted to be played by musical bells.
cabassou: A speciec of armadillo of the genus Xenurus (X. unicinctus and X. hispidus); the tatouay. [Written also Kabassou.]
caloyer: A monk of the Greek Church; a cenobite, anchoret, or recluse of the rule of St. Basil, especially, one on or near Mt. Athos.
catty: An East Indian Weight of 11/3 pounds.
cat: 1. (Zoöl.) An animal of various species of the genera Felis and Lynx. The domestic cat is Felis domestica. The European wild cat (Felis catus) is much larger than the domestic cat. | To bring to the cathead; as, to cat an anchor. See Anchor. Totten.
castrensial: Belonging to a camp. Sir T. Browne.
carnification: The act or process of turning to flesh, or to a substance resembling flesh.
callithumpian: Of, pertaining to, or resembling, a callithump. [U. S.]
calculus: 1. (Med.) Any solid concretion, formed in any part of the body, but most frequent in the organs that act as reservoirs, and in the passages connected with them; as, biliary calculi; urinary calculi, etc. 2. (Math.) A method of computation; any process of reasoning by the use of symbols; any branch of mathematics that may involve calculation.
cathedral: The principal church in a diocese, so called because in it the bishop has his official chair (Cathedra) or throne. | 1. Pertaining to the head church of a diocese; as, a cathedral church; cathedral service. 2. Emanating from the chair of office, as of a pope or bishop; official; authoritative.
camleted: Wavy or undulating like camlet; veined. Sir T. Herbert.
cancel: 1. To inclose or surround, as with a railing, or with latticework. (old) A little obscure place canceled in with iron work is the pillar or stump at which . . . our Savior was scourged. Evelyn. 2. | 1. An inclosure; a boundary; a limit. (old) A prison is but a retirement, and opportunity of serious thoughts, to a person whose spirit . . . desires no enlargement beyond the cancels of the body.
canyada: A small cañon; a narrow valley or glen; also, but less frequently, an open valley. [Local, Western U. S.]
caruncular: Of, pertaining to, or like, a caruncle; furnished with caruncles.
capreoline: Of or pertaining to the roebuck.
cameo: A carving in relief, esp. one on a small scale used as a jewel for personal adornment, or like. Note: Most cameos are carved in a material which has layers of different colors, such stones as the onyx and sardonyx, and various kinds of shells, being used. Cameo conch (Zoöl.), a large, marine, univalve shell, esp. Cassis cameo, C.
captivity: 1. The state of being a captive or a prisoner. More celebrated in his captivity that in his greatest triumphs. Dryden. 2. A state of being under control; subjection of the will or affections; bondage. Sink in the soft captivity together. Addison. Syn. -- Imprisonment; confinement; bondage; subjection; servitude; slavery; thralldom; serfdom.
calvary: 1. The place where Christ was crucified, on a small hill outside of Jerusalem. Luke xxiii. 33. Note: The Latin calvaria is a translation of the Greek Golgotha. Dr. W. Smith. 2.
canyon: A deep gorge, ravine, or gulch, between high and steep banks, worn by water courses. [Mexico & Western U. S.] | The English form of the Spanish word Cañon.
caddy: A small box, can, or chest to keep tea in.
calyciform: Having the form or appearance of a calyx.
catholicness: The quality of being catholic; universality; catholicity.
cantankerous: Perverse; contentious; ugly; malicious. [Colloq.] -- Can*tan"ker*ous*ly, adv. -- Can*tan"ker*ous*ness, n. The cantankerous old maiden aunt. Theckeray.
cassidony: (a) The French lavender (Lawandula Stachas). (b) The goldilocks (Chrysocoma linosyris) and perhaps other plants related to the genus Gnaphalium or cudweed.
caducary: Relating to escheat, forfeiture, or confiscation.
cancelli: 1. An interwoven or latticed wall or inclosure; latticework, rails, or crossbars, as around the bar of a court of justice, between the chancel and the have of a church, or in a window. 2. (Anat.) The interlacing osseous plates constituting the elastic porous tissue of certain parts of the bones, esp. in their articular extremities.
capriped: Having feet like those of a goat.
caseose: A soluble product (proteose) formed in the gastric and pancreatic digestion of casein and caseinogen.
cathedrated: Relating to the chair or office of a teacher. (old)
candytuft: An annual plant of the genus Iberis, cultivated in gardens. The name was originally given to the I. umbellata, first, discovered in the island of Candia.
catskillperiod: The closing subdivision of the Devonian age in America. The rocks of this period are well developed in the Catskill mountains, and extend south and west under the Carboniferous formation. See the Diagram under Geology.
calculation: 1. The act or process, or the result, of calculating; computation; reckoning, estimate. "The calculation of eclipses." Nichol. The mountain is not so his calculation makes it. Boyle. 2. An expectation based on cirumstances. The lazy gossips of the port, Abborrent of a calculation crost, Began to chafe as at a personal wrong. Tennyson.
caledonia: The ancient Latin name of Scotland; -- still used in poetry.
calamint: A genus of perennial plants (Calamintha) of the Mint family, esp. the C. Nepela and C. Acinos, which are called also basil thyme.
capitulary: 1. A capitular. 2. The body of laws or statutes of a chapter, or of an ecclesiastical council. 3. A collection of laws or statutes, civil and ecclesiastical, esp. | Relating to the chapter of a cathedral; capitular. "Capitulary acts." Warton.
caviling: Disposed to cavil; finding fault without good reason. See Captious. His depreciatory and caviling criticism. Lewis.
carnivorous: Eating or feeding on flesh. The term is applied: (a) to animals which naturally seek flesh for food, as the tiger, dog, etc.; (b) to plants which are supposed to absorb animal food; (c) to substances which destroy animal tissue, as caustics.
calking: The act or process of making seems tight, as in ships, or of furnishing with calks, as a shoe, or copying, as a drawing. Calking iron, a tool like a chisel, used in calking ships, tightening seams in ironwork, etc. Their left hand does the calking iron guide. Dryden.
catchcrop: Any crop grown between the rows of another crop or intermediate between two crops in ordinary rotation in point of time. -- Catch"- crop`ping, n. Radishes . . . are often grown as a catch crop with other vegetables. L. H. Bailey.
calendar: 1. An orderly arrangement of the division of time, adapted to the purposes of civil life, as years, months, weeks, and days; also, a register of the year with its divisions; an almanac. 2. | To enter or write in a calendar; to register. Waterhouse.
calcified: Consisting of, or containing, calcareous matter or lime salts; calcareous.
cacolet: A chair, litter, or other contrivance fitted to the back or pack saddle of a mule for carrying travelers in mountainous districts, or for the transportation of the sick and wounded of an army.
calicoback: (a) The calico bass. (b) An hemipterous insect (Murgantia histrionica) which injures the cabbage and other garden plants; -- called also calico bug and harlequin cabbage bug.
calaboose: A prison; a jail. [Local, U. S.]
caballero: A knight or cavalier; hence, a gentleman.
catercousin: A remote relation. See Quater-cousin. Shak.
canal: 1. An artificial channel filled with water and designed for navigation, or for irrigating land, etc. 2. (Anat.) A tube or duct; as, the alimentary canal; the semicircular canals of the ear. Canal boat, a boat for use on a canal; esp. one of peculiar shape, carrying freight, and drawn by horses walking on the towpath beside the canal. Canal lock. See Lock.
cajuputene: A colorlees or greenish oil extracted from cajuput.
cathetus: One line or radius falling perpendicularly on another; as, the catheti of a right-angled triangle, that is, the two sides that include the right angle. Barlow.
cassumunar: A pungent, bitter, aromatic, gingerlike root, obtained from the East Indies.
carburize: To combine wtih carbon or a carbon compound; -- said esp. of a process for conferring a higher degree of illuminating power on combustible gases by mingling them with a vapor of valatile hydrocarbons.
candlemas: The second day of February, on which is celebrated the feast of the Purification of the Virgin Mary; -- so called because the candles for the altar or other sacred uses are blessed on that day.
cadet: 1. The younger of two brothers; a younger brother or son; the youngest son. The cadet of an ancient and noble family. Wood. 2. (Mil.) (a) A gentleman who carries arms in a regiment, as a volunteer, with a view of acquiring military skill and obtaining a commission. (b) A young man in training for military or naval service; esp.
cattail: A tall rush or flag (Typha latifolia) growing in marshes, with long, glat leaves, and having its flowers in a close cylindrical spike at the top of the stem. The leaves are frequently used for seating chairs, making mats, etc. See Catkin. Note: The lesser cat-tail is Typha angustifolia.
cartographer: One who make charts or maps.
cadastre: An official statement of the quantity and value of real estate for the purpose of apportioning the taxes payable on such property.
cauline: Growing immediately on a caulis; of or pertaining to a caulis.
cabinet: 1. A hut; a cottage; a small house. (old) Hearken a while from thy green cabinet, The rural song of careful Colinet. Spenser. 2. A small room, or retired apartment; a closet. 3. | Suitable for a cabinet; small. He [Varnhagen von Ense] is a walking cabinet edition of Goethe. For. Quar. Rev.
caffetannic: Pertaining to, or derived from, the tannin of coffee. Caffetannic acid, a variety of tannin obtained from coffee berries, regarded as a glucoside.
cardioinhibitory: Checking or arresting the heart's action.
calando: (Mus.) Gradually diminishing in rapidity and loudness.
caveat: 1. (Law) A notice given by an interested party to some officer not to do a certain act until the party is heard in opposition; as, a caveat entered in a probate court to stop the proving of a will or the taking out of letters of administration, etc. Bouvier. 2. (U. S.
calcedon: A foul vein, like chalcedony, in some precious stones.
cartway: A way or road for carts.
callosum: The great band commissural fibers which unites the two cerebral hemispheres. See corpus callosum, under Carpus.
categoricalness: The quality of being categorical, positive, or absolute. A. Marvell.
caveating: Shifting the sword from one side of an adversary's sword to the other.
cafeteria: A restaurant or café at which the patrons serve themselves with food kept at a counter, taking the food to small tables to eat. [U. S.]
cadence: 1. The act or state of declining or sinking. (old) Now was the sun in western cadence low. Milton. 2. A fall of the voice in reading or speaking, especially at the end of a sentence. 3. | To regulate by musical measure. These parting numbers, cadenced by my grief. Philips.
carborundumcloth: Cloth or paper covered with powdered carborundum.
cadaverin: A sirupy, nontoxic ptomaine, C5H14N2 (chemically pentamethylene diamine), formed in putrefaction of flesh, etc.
cankerbloom: The bloom or blossom of the wild rose or dog-rose.
castigatory: Punitive in order to amendment; corrective. | An instrument formerly used to punish and correct arrant scolds; -- called also a ducking stool, or trebucket. Blacktone.
canthus: The corner where the upper and under eyelids meet on each side of the eye.
carene: A fast of forty days on bread and water. (old)
cachou: A silvered aromatic pill, used to correct the odor of the breath.
caravel: A name given to several kinds of vessels. (a) The caravel of the 16th century was a small vessel with broad bows, high, narrow poop, four masts, and lateen sails. Columbus commanded three caravels on his great voyage. (b) A Portuguese vessel of 100 or 150 tons burden. (c) A small fishing boat used on the French coast. (d) A Turkish man-of-war.
caecal: 1. Of or pertaining to the cæcum, or blind gut. 2. Having the form of a cæcum, or bag with one opening; baglike; as, the cæcal extremity of a duct.
cannelure: A groove in any cylinder; specif., a groove around the cylinder of an elongated bullet for small arms to contain a lubricant, or around the rotating band of a gun projectile to lessen the resistance offered to the rifling. Also, a groove around the base of a cartridge, where the extractor takes hold. --Can"ne*lured (#), a.
cascarasagrada: Holy bark; the bark of the California buckthorn (Rhamnus Purshianus), used as a mild cathartic or laxative.
catchment: A surface of ground on which water may be caught and collected into a reservoir.
cabezon: A California fish (Hemilepidotus spinosus), allied to the sculpin.
calabash: 1. The common gourd (plant or fruit). 2. The fruit of the calabash tree. 3. A water dipper, bottle, backet, or other utensil, made from the dry shell of a calabash or gourd. Calabash tree. (Bot.), a tree of tropical America (Crescentia cujete), producing a large gourdike fruit, containing a purgative pulp.
caufle: A gung of slaves. Same as Coffle.
capling: The cap or coupling of a flail, through which the thongs pass which connect the handle and swingel. Wright.
carnally: According to the flesh, to the world, or to human nature; in a manner to gratify animal appetites and lusts; sensually. For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace. Rom. viii. 6.
cassavawood: A West Indian tree (Turpinia occidentalis) of the family Staphyleaceæ.
cannular: Having the form of a tube; tubular. [Written also canular.]
camarasaurus: A genus of gigantic American Jurassic dinosaurs, having large cavities in the bodies of the dorsal vertebræ.
camaieu: 1. A cameo. (old) Crabb. 2. (Fine Arts) Painting in shades of one color; monochrome. Mollett.
candidate: One who offers himself, or is put forward by others, as a suitable person or an aspirant or contestant for an office, privilege, or honor; as, a candidate for the office of governor; a candidate for holy orders; a candidate for scholastic honors.
catchbasin: A cistern or vault at the point where a street gutter discharges into a sewer, to oatch bulky matters which would not pass readly throught the sewer. Knight.
canthook: A wooden lever with a movable iron hook. hear the end; -- used for canting or turning over heavy logs, etc. [U. S.] Bartlett.
cachemia: A degenerated or poisoned condition of the blood. --Ca*chæ"mic, Ca*che"mic (#), a.
catechu: A dry, brown, astringent extract, obtained by decoction and evaporation from the Acacia catechu, and several other plants growing in India. It contains a large portion of tannin or tannic acid, and is used in medicine and in the arts. It is also known by the names terra japonica, cutch, gambier, etc. Ure. Dunglison.
cashew: A tree (Anacardium occidentale) of the same family which the sumac. It is native in tropical America, but is now naturalized in all tropical countries. Its fruit, a kidney-shaped nut, grows at the extremity of an edible, pear-shaped hypocarp, about three inches long.
candlewaster: One who consumes candles by being up late for study or dissipation. A bookworm, a candlewaster. B. Jonson.

capital: 1. Of or pertaining to the head. (old) Needs must the Serpent now his capital bruise Expect with mortal pain. Milton. 2. The head or uppermost member of a column, pilaster, etc. It consists generally of three parts, abacus, bell (or vase), and necking. See these terms, and Column. 2. Etym: [Cf. F.
catalan: Of or pertaining to Catalonia. -- n. A native or inbabitant of Catalonia; also, the language of Catalonia. Catalan furnace, Catalan forge (Metal.), a kind of furnace for producing wrought iron directly from the ore. It was formerly much used, esp. in Catalonia, and is still used in some parts of the United States and elsewhere.
cashmere: 1. A rich stuff for shawls, acaris, etc., originally made in Cashmere from the soft wool found beneath the hair of the goats of Cashmere, Thibet, and the Himalayas. Some cashmere, of fine quality, is richly embroidered for sale to Europeans. 2. A dress fabric made of fine wool, or of fine wool and cotton, in imitation of the original cashmere.
cankerous: Affecting like a canker. "Canrerous shackles." Thomson. Misdeem it not a cankerous change. Wordsworth.
cartilage: A translucent, elastic tissue; gristle. Note: Cartilage contains no vessels, and consists of a homogeneous, intercellular matrix, in which there are numerous minute cavities, or capsules, containing protoplasmic cells, the cartilage corpuscul. See Illust under Duplication. Articular cartilage, cartilage that lines the joints.
carburet: To combine or to impregnate with carbon, as by passing through or over a liquid hydrocarbon; to carbonize or carburize. By carbureting the gas you may use poorer coal. Knight.
carnival: 1. A festival celebrated with merriment and revelry in Roman Gatholic countries during the week before Lent, esp. at Rome and Naples, during a few days (three to ten) before Lent, ending with Shrove Tuesday. The carnival at Venice is everywhere talked of. Addison. 2. Any merrymaking, feasting, or masquerading, especially when overstepping the bounds of decorum;
cassideous: Helmet-shaped; -- applied to a corolla having a broad, helmet- shaped upper petal, as in aconite.
calla: A genus of plants, of the order Araceæ. Note: The common Calla of cultivation is Richardia Africana, belonging to another genus of the same order. Its large spathe is pure white, surrounding a fleshy spike, which is covered with minute apetalous flowers.
calculous: 1. Of the nature of a calculus; like stone; gritty; as, a calculous concretion. Sir T. Browne. 2. Caused, or characterized, by the presence of a calculus or calculi; a, a calculous disorder; affected with gravel or stone; as, a calculous person.
capitulum: 1. A thick head of flowers on a very short axis, as a clover top, or a dandelion; a composite flower. A capitulum may be either globular or flat. Gray. 2. (Anat.) A knobike protuberance of any part, esp. at the end of a bone or cartilage. Note: [See Illust. of Artiodactyla.]
cask: 1. Same as Casque. (old) 2. A barrel-shaped vessel made of staves headings, and hoops, usually fitted together so as to hold liquids. It may be larger or smaller than a barrel. 3. The quantity contained in a cask. 4. A casket; a small box for jewels. (old) Shak.
castanets: Two small, concave shells of ivory or hard wood, shaped like spoons, fastened to the thumb, and beaten together with the middle finger; -- used by the Spaniards and Moors as an accompaniment to their dance and guitars. Note: The singular, castanet, is used of one of the pair, or, sometimes, of the pair forming the instrument.
calorification: Production of heat, esp. animal heat.
carnal: 1. Of or pertaining to the body or is appetites; animal; fleshly; sensual; given to sensual indulgence; lustful; human or worldly as opposed to spiritual. For ye are yet carnal. 1 Car. iii. 3. Not sunk in carnal pleasure. Milton rnal desires after miracles. Trench. 2. Flesh-devouring; cruel; ravenous; bloody. (old) This carnal cur Preys on the issue of his mother's body. Shak.
calcareosiliceous: Consisting of, or containing calcareous and siliceous earths.
cabin: 1. A cottage or small house; a hut. Swift. A hunting cabin in the west. E. Everett. 2. A small room; an inclosed place. So long in secret cabin there he held Her captive. Spenser. 3. | To live in, or as in, a cabin; to lodge. I'll make you . . . cabin in a cave. Shak.
carpentry: 1. The art of cutting, framing, and joining timber, as in the construction of buildings. 2. An assemblage of pieces of timber connected by being framed together, as the pieces of a roof, floor, etc.; work done by a carpenter.
carditis: Inflammation of the fleshy or muscular substance of the heart. See Endocardris and Pericarditis. Dunglison.
cajole: To deceive with flattery or fair words; to wheedle. I am not about to cajole or flatter you into a reception of my views. F. W. Robertson. Syn. -- To flatter; wheedle; delude; coax; entrap.
cathartic: 1. (Med.) Cleansing the bowels; promoting evacuations by stool; purgative. 2. Of or pertaining to the purgative principle of senna, as cathartic acid. | A medicine that promotes alvine discharges; a purge; a purgative of moderate activity. Note: The cathartics are more energetic and certain in action that the laxatives, which simply increase the…
cappadine: A floss or waste obtained from the cocoon after the silk has been reeled off, used for shag.
cartography: The act business of forming chart's or maps.
cathole: One of two small holes astern, above the gunroom ports, through which hawsers may be passed.
canonry: A benefice or prebend in a cathedral or collegiate church; a right to a place in chapter and to a portion of its revenues; the dignity or emoluments of a canon.
calfskin: The hide or skin of a calf; or leather made of the skin.
cantref: A district comprising a hundred villages, as in Wales. [Written also kantry.]
caseharden: 1. To subject to a process which converts the surface of iron into steel. 2. To render insensible to good influences.
causal: Relating to a cause or causes; inplying or containing a cause or causes; expressing a cause; causative. Causal propositions are where two propositions are joined by causal words. Watts. | A causal word or form of speech. Anglo-Saxon drencan to drench, causal of Anglo-Saxon drincan to drink. Skeat.
callisection: Painless vivisection; -- opposed to sentisection. B. G. Wilder.
cantoncrape: A soft, white or colored silk fabric, of a gauzy texture and wavy appearance, used for ladies' scarfs, shawls, bonnet trimmings, etc.; -- called also Oriental crape. De Colange.
carambola: An East Indian tree (Averrhoa Carambola), and its acid, juicy fruit; called also Coromandel gooseberry.
carpus: The wrist; the bones or cartilages between the forearm, or antibrachium, and the hand or forefoot; in man, consisting of eight short bones disposed in two rows.
cardialgy: A burning or gnawing pain, or feeling of distress, referred to the region of the heart, accompanied with cardisc palpitation; heartburn. It is usually a symptom of indigestion.
cachet: A seal, as of a letter. Lettre de cachet Etym: [F.], a sealed letter, especially a letter or missive emanating from the sovereign; -- much used in France before the Revolution as an arbitrary order of imprisonment.
cacostomia: Diseased or gangrenous condition of the mouth.
carboxide: A compound of carbon and oxygen, as carbonyl, with some element or radical; as, potassium carboxide. Potassium carboxide, a grayish explosive crystalline compound, C6O6K, obtained by passing carbon monoxide over heated potassium.
calcographical: Relating to, or in the style of, calcography.
cabiric: Of or pertaining to the Cabiri, or to their mystical worship. [Written also Cabiritic.]
catalpa: A genus of American and East Indian trees, of which the best know species are the Catalpa bignonioides, a large, ornamental North American tree, with spotted white flowers and long cylindrical pods, and the C. speciosa, of the Mississipi valley; -- called also Indian bean.
cavort: To prance ostentatiously; -- said of a horse or his rider. [Local slang U. S.]
cancelier: To turn in flight; -- said of a hawk. (old) Nares. He makes his stoop; but wanting breath, is forced To cancelier. Massinger. | The turn of a hawk upon the wing to recover herself, when she misses her aim in the stoop. (old) The fierce and eager hawks, down thrilling from the skies, Make sundry canceliers are they the fowl…
cardiography: 1. Description of the heart. 2. (Physiol.) Examination by the cardiograph.
cannonier: A man who manages, or fires, cannon.
camlet: A woven fabric originally made of camel's hair, now chiefly of goat's hair and silk, or of wool and cotton. [Sometimes written camelot and camblet.] Note: They have been made plain and twilled, of sigle warp and weft, of double warp, and sometimes with double weft also, with thicker yarn. Beck (Draper's Dict. )
catherinewheel: 1. (Geoth.Arth.) Same as Rose window and Wheel window. Called also Catherine- wheel window. 2. (Pyrotechny) A revolving piece of fireworks resembling in form the window of the same name. [Written also Catharine wheel.]
caterwaul: To cry as cats in rutting time; to make a harsh, offensive noise. Coleridge.
carrion: 1. The dead and putrefying body or flesh of an animal; flesh so corrupted as to be unfit for food. They did eat the dead carrions. Spenser. 2. A contemptible or worthless person; | Of or pertaining to dead and putrefying carcasses; feeding on carrion. A prey for carrion kites. Shak. Carrion beetle (Zoöl.), any beetle that feeds habitually on dead animals;
causerie: Informal talk or discussion, as about literary matters; light conversation; chat.
catcall: A sound like the cry of a cat, such as is made in playhouses to express dissatisfaction with a play; also, a small shrill instrument for making such a noise. Upon the rising of the curtain. I was very much surprised with the great consort of catcalls which was exhibited. Addison.
caprice: 1. An abrupt change in feeling, opinion, or action, proceeding from some whim or fancy; a freak; a notion. "Caprices of appetite." W. Irving. 2. (Mus.) See Capriccio. Syn. -- Freak; whim; crotchet; fancy; vagary; humor; whimsey; fickleness.
catallacta: A division of Protozoa, of which Magosphæra is the type. They exist both in a myxopod state, with branched pseudopodia, and in the form of ciliated bodies united in free, spherical colonies.
castillan: Of or pertaining to Castile, in Spain.
